name: n4_px_binding_audit
description: Report the Px bindings whose ORD does not resolve (station-audits S15), read-only. Without file_ord it audits every Px view below root (the n4_list_px_views query, up to max_views), each relative ORD (slot:a, slot:../a, ../a) read against the component the view is on; with file_ord it audits that one .px file, relative ORDs read against base when given. A binding is the ord attribute of an element whose tag ends in Binding (ValueBinding, ActionBinding, kitPx and vendor bindings), widget being the nearest enclosing element with a name. Each distinct target is loaded once over BOX (a trailing |slot: hop dropped): one that loads resolves; one that does not is missing only when proven, i.e. its deepest ancestor that loads holds no slot by the next name, neither loaded nor declared by its type contract. Anything else is unknown with why, never counted as broken: another scheme (history:, file:, module:, ...), a chained ORD, a relative ORD with no base, a handle (h:) that does not load, a timeout or hidden station error whose parent still holds the name. Reply: views [{px_file, base, status (ok, not_found, forbidden, truncated, unparsable, no_file), bindings, error?}], broken and unknown [{px_file, widget, element, ord (as written), target (absolute ORD or null), why}], counts {views, bindings, unique_targets, resolves, missing, unknown} (per binding, except unique_targets), truncated (views past max_views or bindings past max_bindings were not audited) and elapsed_ms. One BQL read, one GET per .px file, then one load per distinct target and per ancestor walked. Read-only.

root.description: Slot ORD below which every Px view is audited (default: the whole station); ignored with file_ord

file_ord.description: Audit only this .px file: file:^px/General.px or px/General.px

base.description: With file_ord: the slot ORD relative binding ORDs are read against (the component the view is on), e.g. station:|slot:/Plant/AHU1

max_bindings.description: Most bindings audited across all views

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout in seconds of each .px read
